doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Accompanying singers: Betty Carter and Joe Williams
summary: Playing for singers demands flexibility and sensitivity; Betty Carter sang like a horn player and Joe Williams worked high-class rooms.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Working with singers, you’re going to go from you may be playing the same tune with two different singers but one’s a man and one’s a woman, and you’ve got to know — you’ve got to be flexible, right? You’ve got to play it in A flat instead of E flat?

Right. Oh yeah. Oh that’s it. You’ve definitely got to be flexible. And then you know, but working with singers, it’s a good experience for keyboard players. Because when you’re playing with a band you could be more forceful. But for high singers you’ve got to be sensitive and you’ve really got to listen. So that’s a good experience for you. But I’ll tell you one thing, man, working with Betty Carter, Monk, that was interesting. Because Betty Carter was like a horn player. Because you know she based her singing on horn players and then so with Betty you could just play. So you know Betty Carter, that’s really a great opportunity.
Well actually you mentioned Joe Williams and he helped us get this project started that we’re doing.

Okay. Oh yeah Joe was something because he’s the champion of Count Basie and all the experiences. And then you know Joe Williams, he worked what I’d say more high class venues and rooms. So it was great. Because like you say he was with Count Basie and Vegas, he’s been everywhere.
